title: Ecclesiastes Bible Quiz - Chapter 8
description: Ten questions on Ecclesiastes 8: keeping the king's command, the limits of man's power, and why it will be better with those who fear God.

questions.text: According to the opening verse, what does a man's wisdom do to his face?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 8:1 says that a man's wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.

answers.text: It makes his face grow pale
It makes his face shine
It makes his face look old
It hides his face from others

questions.text: Why does the speaker say, "Keep the king's command"?
questions.explanation: The speaker says to keep the king's command because of the oath to God.

answers.text: Because the king rewards the obedient
Because the king's servants are watching
Because the law of the land requires it
Because of the oath to God

questions.text: What does this chapter say about the king's word?
questions.explanation: The king's word is supreme, and no one can say to him, "What are you doing?"

answers.text: It is supreme
It is quickly forgotten
It is often broken
It is written in a book

questions.text: Over what does no man have power, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: There is no man who has power over the spirit to contain the spirit, neither does he have power over the day of death.

answers.text: The king's treasures
The wind and the sea
The day of death
The city gates

questions.text: Why is the heart of the sons of men fully set in them to do evil?
questions.explanation: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.

answers.text: Because they have never heard of God
Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily
Because the king commands them to do evil
Because the righteous refuse to warn them

questions.text: Even though a sinner commits crimes a hundred times and lives long, with whom does the speaker say it will surely be better?
questions.explanation: The speaker says he surely knows it will be better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him.

answers.text: Those who fear God
Those who serve the king
Those who grow rich
Those who live in the city

questions.text: What vanity done on the earth does the speaker describe concerning righteous men and wicked men?
questions.explanation: There are righteous men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked, and wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous; the speaker calls this vanity.

answers.text: The righteous and the wicked both forget all the works they have done
The righteous become wicked in old age, and the wicked become righteous
The righteous and the wicked never meet each other on the earth
Righteous men receive what fits the work of the wicked, and the other way around

questions.text: What did the speaker commend, saying a man has no better thing under the sun?
questions.explanation: The speaker commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun than to eat, to drink, and to be joyful.

answers.text: Silence
Hard labor
Mirth
Long life

questions.text: What happened to the wicked whom the speaker saw buried?
questions.explanation: The speaker saw the wicked buried, and they went and were forgotten in the city where they did this; this also is vanity.

answers.text: They were honored with great monuments
They were forgotten in the city
They were mourned for many days
They were buried outside the city

questions.text: According to the end of the chapter, can a wise man find out the work that is done under the sun?
questions.explanation: Even though a wise man thinks he can comprehend it, he won't be able to find it; man can't find out the work that is done under the sun.

answers.text: Yes, if he labors long enough to seek it out
Yes, but only when he reaches his old age
Only if the king gives him his help
No, he won't be able to find it
